newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 28.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:

* Super Bowl XXXI on News Corp's Fox Broadcasting earned a 43.3 rating and a 65 share, according to Nielsen Media Research, making it the 17th-highest rated Super Bowl contest seen at least in part by a record 128.9 million viewers.
* The Screen Actors Guild has begun a study to examine the issue of declining compensation for recognizable, second-tier actors.

* Starting March 3, Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS will give a rest to 9 p.m. sitcom "Murphy Brown" and move "Cybill" to that slot from the 9:30 p.m. slot. "Ink" will move to 9:30, and "Everybody Loves Raymond," will go Mondays at 8:30 following "Cosby."
* Allen & Albert Hughes are directing a documentary about American pimps and are negotiating to sign with a distributor, hoping to have the film in theaters by August.
* Michael Grade has resigned as chief executive of British television network Channel 4.
* Oscar-winning actor Denzel Washington will receive actor-of-the-year honors at ShoWest '97.
